name: Painting PC
summary: Painting PC is a PC-port of OISOI's Painting VR game. The game keeps a handful of the game's brushes and its realistic painting experience. Additionally the game includes a commission system where people ask you to paint something specific whereafter you gain currency and followers that progress you through the game.
contributions: For Painting PC, besides a quick hand here and there during polish, I was the only programmer working on the project. Thus besides the already existing brushes and painting system, I worked on every aspect of the game.

highlights.title: Commissions system
highlights.description: In the game players can accept commissions from clients in their phone. These are small conversations the player has with the client with potential diverging paths.

highlights.title: Game savefile system
highlights.description: Since the player was able to progress in the game I had to create a savefile system.

name: Painting VR
summary: Painting VR is the most rated painting simulation app on the Meta VR platform. It has an extensive set of brushes and tools and allows for highly realistic brush strokes. Players can also enjoy painting in a handful of diverse environments. The game gets frequently updated with new features, brushes and tools.
contributions:
When I started my internship at OISOI this is the game I was initially put on, I helped clear out bugs and polish existing features. Over time I was allowed to develop new features, first with a co-programmer, then on my own. When I officially started working at OISOI I was put on other projects, but every now and then I was placed back to help the lead developer finish some bigger updates. 
The game is made using Unity, so I mainly used C# during development.

highlights.title: Brush packs
highlights.description: I developed the system behind buying in-game brush packs. These were DLC's that added a pack of new brushes to the game which you could access from your inventory.

highlights.title: Canvas starters
highlights.description: An empty canvas can be quite intimidating, stopping players from painting anything. To resolve that issue I developed canvas starters. These are random shapes and blobs that can be cycled through that will then be printed onto the canvas when created. The blobs were made using metaballs which I learned to use earlier in my internship.

highlights.title: Paint bucket metaballs
highlights.description: In my internship I asked to work on something graphics programming related. I was allowed to try and improve the existing paint bucket's pouring mechanic by using metaballs. I managed to get a rough prototype working, but we decided to scrap it since it still needed some development-time which we didn't have.

highlights.title: Brush importer tool
highlights.description: One of my tasks during the internship was to make a tool that would make it easier to create new brushes. The tool was made using Unity uGUI and got used when creating brush packs with simpler brushes.

name: Wait What's That
summary: Wait What's That (WWT) is a multiplayer VR pictionary game where the drawer needs to draw a word with a random twist and tool. These can range from drawing on a tv with a rubber chicken, to spraying on a canvas where your sprayed lines constantly disappear.
contributions: At first I was placed on WWT for only a short while to help with the final polish steps before release. Then later when the player count started going up I returned to fix a bunch of bugs. After I mainly worked as solo dev (I got some help towards the end of the bigger updates) to implement a new dedicated lobby environment, as well as implementing handtracking including some new tools.

highlights.title: Social lobby
highlights.description: To help players connect with each other so they can play games together, we decided to implement a social lobby hosted by a dedicated server. I worked on setting up the server on a virtual machine, and made sure players correctly connected to it.

highlights.title: Handtracking
highlights.description: The studio signed a contract with Meta to implement handtracking into WWT, I was in lead for this assignment. The player's fingers and hands were tracked and made the character's hands move. This also needed to be synchronised, so some time was spent making sure the syncing didn't take too much bandwith.

highlights.title: Best Belgian multiplayer game
highlights.description: WWT got nominated to, and won, the Best Belgian Multiplayer Game Award in 2025 where we competed against 2 other games.

name: Vandalizer
summary: Vandalizer is a high quality multiplayer VR grafitti game where you can spray paint on different objects. Each object is contained within a card which you can unlock by playing.
contributions: I helped develop this game when it was in its earlier phases and was supposed to be a different game. I mainly worked on smaller features and fixing bugs.

highlights.title: Highlight spots
highlights.description: The game used to be split in a creator- and spectator-mode. In creator-mode you could spray an artwork in an environment, take a picture and upload it. I made it so that these pictures would pop up when close to the original picture's location. You could then replay the artwork's creation and like it.

name: Project Kame
summary: Project Kame is the last group project I made in DAE. We were commissioned by 2 people to create a prototype of a game idea they had to potentially start their indie studio with. The game is a platformer where you try to reach the end of the level before the timer runs out. The player gets stronger every time they die by power-ups they gain after losing.
contributions: In this project we were with 2 programmers, I mainly worked on the enemies in the game, the swimming movement, the power-up system and the game loop system.
